key_insight: Euclidean Fast Attention introduces a linear‑scaling attention mechanism using Euclidean rotary encodings, enabling accurate global atomic representations for 3D data while avoiding the quadratic cost of standard attention.
problem_solved: Overcomes the O(N^2) computational and memory cost of standard attention for 3D atomic systems, making it feasible to model long‑range physical interactions at scale.
method: Use Euclidean rotary encodings to make attention operations compatible with 3D rotations and translations (geometric equivariance).
Reformulate attention into a fast, linearized computation that reduces complexity from quadratic to linear (or near‑linear) in the number of atoms/points.
Combine the linear attention with global atomic representations to capture long‑range physical effects efficiently and accurately.
impact: Makes high‑fidelity, physics‑aware ML for large molecular and materials systems computationally practical, reducing compute and memory requirements while preserving accuracy for long‑range interactions.
visual_elements: Scaling comparison plot: quadratic vs linear attention (time/memory vs number of atoms).
Illustration of Euclidean rotary encoding: vector rotations in 3D showing equivariance under rotation/translation.
Atomic system diagram: long‑range connections highlighted to show global attention vs local message passing.
Benchmark chart: accuracy vs speed/memory across baseline attention and Euclidean Fast Attention on representative datasets.
paper_title: Machine learning global atomic representations with Euclidean fast attention
paper_authors: J. Thorben Frank, Stefan Chmiela, Klaus-Robert Müller, Oliver T. Unke
